issues.text: A gap of my own step 05c, found by the probe SP1 of this step (for ORCH; tools/test/e2e/pixel-office.e2e.js is not in this write set, so it is not edited here). The step-05c form in 'isolated start' collects the names of the recorded hook env with Object.keys, so a hook helper that gives the three right names on an object whose prototype is the whole environment passes it (SP1: isolated start green), while spawn hands every inherited name to the child (measured in self_check). The step-05 form, assert.deepEqual of the whole object, failed it by its prototype check. The suite still catches SP1 through E2K-50 (the bare read of the whole environment in the spec: red), but 'isolated start' alone no longer does. The fix is the same as here: collect the names by for…in and assert a plain prototype and no symbol keys, as envShape does in e2e-stand.test.js. Proposal: ORCH adds the spec to a write set (this launch can do it at once) or gives it to step 05e as a finding.

E2S-05 still names the expected names in its red output (the base names this process has: PATH, TMPDIR, LANG and so on, the given SAI_FAKE_* names, HOME, USERPROFILE): they are the names the test expects, not other variables of the process, and no value is printed. E2K-37 names only its two own names, because there the expected names are the whole environment of this process.

The full check ran in the tool's background and I waited for it within my turn (a watch on its done file); nothing heavy ran meanwhile. One harness at a time, one Chrome at a time, caffeinate -i, no busy loops. The criterion word 'picker-office' of step 05c was ORCH's typo (ORCH's message), as read there.
